chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abu Nasr narrated from Abu al-Hasan al-Mausili, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him)

He said: A rabbi came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and asked: 'O Commander of the Faithful, did you see your Lord when you worshipped Him?' He replied: 'Woe to you! I do not worship a Lord whom I cannot see.' The rabbi asked: 'How do you see Him?' He replied: 'Woe to you! The eyes do not perceive Him through the vision of sight, but the hearts see Him through the realities of faith.'
ai.seo_question: How do Muslims see God according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* articulates the core Shia doctrine of *ru'yat al-qulub* (vision of the heart), distinguishing it from physical sight (*basar*). Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while God’s essence is beyond the grasp of physical eyes, as affirmed in Surah Al-An'am, the faithful perceive Him through the inner certainty of the heart, a concept deeply rooted in the debate between the Shia and other schools regarding the beatific vision.
